verdict: Bengaluru's froth risk is broadly flat vs mid-June 2026 with a hotter supply-mix skew: Q2 2026 launches came in ~96% priced ≥₹80L (up from ~68% premium share in Q1) even as overall inventory eased and balance-sheet risk stayed benign. Fundamentals remain sound — housing GNPA fell to ~1.0% at RBI's June 2026 FSR (multi-decade low), pan-India months-of-inventory near ~12, and RBI held repo at 5.25% — but the asking-vs-guidance gap in prime pockets like Indiranagar is now 50–80%, mid-income supply is being crowded out, and Knight Frank's H1 2026 affordability index shows Bengaluru EMI/income worsened from 34% to 35%. Two-speed market: banking system healthy, developer-led luxury concentration keeps the froth flag flying.

indicators.name: Unsold inventory overhang
indicators.value: ~12 months / pan-India ~5.8 quarters; Bengaluru ~58,900 unsold units
indicators.note: Bengaluru overhang held near ~12 months on ~58,900 unsold units; pan-India quarters-to-sell stable at ~5.8 quarters. Absorption keeping pace with a 41% YoY jump in Q2 2026 launches, so the ratio hasn't blown out despite the supply surge.

indicators.name: Launch mix skew to luxury
indicators.note: Bengaluru Q2 2026 saw ~21,670 new units launched (up 41% YoY) with >90% (reported at ~96%) in premium/luxury segments (≥₹80L). Skew has worsened from the ~68% premium share flagged in Q1 — mid/affordable supply is being crowded out.
indicators.src: NewsFirst Prime citing Q2 2026 launch data

indicators.name: EMI-to-income (affordability)
indicators.value: EMI/income 35% H1 2026 vs 34% H2 2025; repo held at 5.25%
indicators.note: Knight Frank Affordability Index H1 2026: Bengaluru's EMI-to-income ratio worsened marginally from 34% to 35% — still comfortably below the 50% stress line but the cushion is eroding. RBI held repo at 5.25% at its June 2026 MPC after cumulative 125 bps of cuts; typical home-loan rates 7.65–8.50%.
indicators.src: Knight Frank India Affordability Index H1 2026; RBI MPC June 2026

indicators.name: Housing-loan defaults (NPAs)
indicators.note: RBI Financial Stability Report June 2026: overall bank GNPAs at 1.8% (multi-decade low), projected to edge to 1.9% by FY28. Housing loans remain the cleanest segment at ~1.0% GNPA (down from ~1.3% in Dec 2025). Secured retail 0.7%, unsecured 1.7%. RBI flagged unsecured retail composition risk, not housing.

indicators.name: Asking vs registered price gap
indicators.value: Indiranagar asking 50–80% over guidance; Devanahalli/Hoskote gap 15–25%
indicators.note: Wide asking-vs-guidance gaps persist in prime pockets — Indiranagar market runs ~50–80% over guidance (guidance ~₹12k/sqft vs market ₹18–22k/sqft); newer corridors (Devanahalli, Hoskote) narrower at 15–25%. No fresh guidance-value hike May–July 2026, but Feb 2026 6–15% urban hike (12–15% Devanahalli/Yelahanka/Hebbal) plus Aug 2025 doubling of registration fee (1%→2%) continue to work through. Total statutory cost ~7.5–7.6% on flats >₹45L.
indicators.src: Squareyards Bangalore rates; OneCity guidance-value tracker

indicators.name: Registration volumes
indicators.value: No fresh June 2026 aggregate published; digital e-stamp live Jan 2026
indicators.note: Karnataka Stamp (Digital e-Stamp) Rules operationalised Jan 2026; Kaveri 2.0 upgrade underway. Registration fee doubled to 2% (Aug 2025) + Feb 2026 guidance hike likely dampened transaction counts in Q1–Q2 2026, but no June 2026 aggregate stamp-duty collection figure was publicly reported at time of check. Cost-driven softening likely.
